global_issues.title: Sticky August CPI cements Fed rate-hike odds
global_issues.note: Confirmed: August CPI rose 0.4% m/m (3.4% y/y), core 0.3% m/m (2.4% y/y), above forecast. CME FedWatch/futures odds of a hike at next week's FOMC meeting jumped from ~70% to 85-90% (CNBC, CBS News, Benzinga, Sept 11). Fed decision itself has not happened yet — briefing correctly frames this as raised odds, not a confirmed hike.

global_issues.title: Middle East conflict escalates oil prices
global_issues.note: Directionally correct (Iran/Houthi attacks, Strait of Hormuz tensions, US strikes on Iranian tankers are real and ongoing), but the price level is overstated/stale. Real-time reporting (CBS, CNN, Yahoo Finance, Sept 9-12) puts Brent in the $97-101/bbl range — a 6-7 week high, not near $120. The 'risk of $120/bbl' framing appears to reference an older or more extreme scenario; no current source supports $120 being the market's near-term priced risk as of Sept 11-12.

missing_major_news.impact: All watchlist names, especially rate-sensitive tech (NVDA, MSFT, MU, CRWD) and high-multiple growth names (PLTR, TSLA) — the briefing discusses hike odds but doesn't flag that the decision itself is imminent (within days), which is the dominant near-term catalyst

missing_major_news.title: US gasoline prices surged to ~$4.22/gallon, highest since June — direct consumer inflation/spending read-through
missing_major_news.impact: Broader market mood context; relevant to consumer-facing/discretionary sentiment not directly in this watchlist but affects the 'paradox' narrative the briefing describes

missing_major_news.impact: Underlying driver of the oil spike the briefing cites — omitting the breakdown in negotiations means the briefing understates how fluid/negative the escalation risk is

market_mood_check.note: S&P 500 actually rose 0.86% to 7,656.98 on Sept 11 (Dow +0.98%, Nasdaq +0.96%) despite the CPI print and oil spike — this matches the briefing's 'closed higher despite sticky CPI... and oil spiking' paradox framing. Yellow/cautiously-mixed traffic light with score 71.3 is consistent with a market that's still grinding higher but facing rate and geopolitical headwinds.

sector_check.note: Leaders/laggards list is plausible given known trends (NVDA, MU, CRWD, MSFT strength; GOOGL, ANET weakness have some support in recent coverage), but the 'rotation toward energy and utilities' claim could not be independently confirmed via search — no current article specifically documents a rotation into energy/utilities this week tied to power-demand names. grok_report.summary: Core macro narrative (sticky CPI raising Fed hike odds, S&P still closing higher, oil rising on Middle East escalation) is well-supported by current reporting, and the NVDA price point checks out exactly against Sept 11 close data. The main flaw is the oil issue overstating price level/risk ($120 vs. actual ~$97-101/bbl) and omitting that the imminent FOMC decision itself (next week) and the breakdown in US-Iran Hormuz talks are the more material near-term catalysts not surfaced in the briefing.
